newsitem.title: USA: U.S., EU hold talks on Cuba investment agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S., EU hold talks on Cuba investment agreement.

text.p: U.S. And European officials held a round of talks this week on implementing an April agreement to settle a dispute over a U.S. law aimed at discouraging foreign investment in Cuba.
"This was a candid and constructive exchange of views on several questions covered by the understanding," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement.

"The issues discussed included disciplines on acquisitions of investments expropriated in contravention of international law and subsequent dealings in covered investments, and principles for addressing issues of conflicting jurisdictions," he added.

Burns said the discussions, which were led on the U.S. side by Assistant Secretary of State Alan Larson, were exploratory. The U.S. objective, he said, is to achieve an agreement on dealing with property in third countries that have been expropriated without compensation.

The April agreement helped defuse a dispute between the United States and the European Union over the so-called Helms-Burton law that seeks to punish foreign companies investing in properties confiscated by the Cuban government after President Fidel Castro took power in 1959.
Burns said negotiators will meet again in July to continue discussion.
